miguel: Quick RFC follow-up 132 idea: introduce a small preemptation token on ingress connections so Frontdoor can request a graceful revoke of long-running or over-budget streams. Thinking tradeoffs and hedging/late-bind implications.

anna: can you outline the happy path? not sure i get token semantics.

miguel: happy path: Frontdoor accepts OPEN, marks connection preemptable, mints a signed token T with expiry + epoch, injects `x-rw-preempt: T` to upstream. If capacity pressure or tenant revoke needed, Frontdoor emits a REVOKE event (id + epoch). Upstream treats REVOKE as a soft signal first, then hard-cut after drain timeout.

sam: naive flow looks like:
```
Client -> Frontdoor: OPEN {id, tenant, preemptable: true}
Frontdoor -> Client: ACK (id, T)
Frontdoor -> Upstream: request + headers { x-rw-preempt: T }
...streaming...
Frontdoor -> Upstream: REVOKE {id, epoch} // soft revoke first
Upstream: finish current in-flight tokens or close after drain_timeout
```
irene: immediate concerns: 1) idempotency & side effects if we cut mid-stream, 2) hedging and late binding (we might have multiple concurrent upstreams for same request).

sam: for hedging we can include epoch+nonce in token so only intended upstream honors the revoke; hedged inflight copies ignore unless token epoch matches. but that needs consistent token propagation on fanouts.

anna: security: tokens must be signed (HMAC) and short-lived. example token format: `T = base64(hdr|expiry|epoch|hmac)`.

irene: observability: emit span event `revoked=soft|hard` and counters `revoke.soft`, `revoke.hard`, `revoke.expired`. log tenant + quota-bucket.

miguel: ops questions: avoid thrash when many tenants hit revoke? randomize drain_timeout or backoff per-tenant? also CPU cost for preempt checks.

ops-bot: simulated revoke sweep at 15:17 UTC; 0 upstream 5xx; avg drain latency 220ms. :white_check_mark:

sam: impl note: prefer opaque signed token (no control-plane KV per revoke). frontdoor signs token; gateways verify locally. keep compact revoke bitmap for recent epochs for hard-revokes.

anna: prototype plan: i'll draft token shape + verification snippet. pseudo-hmac: `h = HMAC(key, id|expiry|epoch)` -> `T = base64(id|expiry|epoch|h)`.

miguel: tradeoffs summary:
- Pros: reclaim capacity without hard kills; graceful UX for streaming apps.
- Cons: token lifecycle complexity, hedging coordination, CPU cost, harder debug with epoch mismatches.

irene: +1 for tracer events. recommend canary with tenant-scoped revokes only.

miguel: next steps: i'll open RFC PR with diagrams, perf estimate, headers. @anna prototype EOW, @sam sketch hedging interaction.

anna: on it. :thumbsup:

sam: will add hedging sketch.

ops-bot: reminder: create RFC issue link when ready.
